data.name: SABT_Text_Configuration
data.value:
Anything from **one** to **four** motors are supported. These can be used separately such that each belt is driven by its own motor with roughly **10Kg** of force; or paired up to double that to **20Kg** (on the **shoulder belts** only).
Use the configuration table above to indicate how you want your motors to behave: • **Mapping**: Which belt a motor is allocated to (**unused**, **left shoulder**, **right shoulder**, **left waist**, **right waist**) • **Direction**: Which direction the motors should turn to apply tension to the belts • **Temperatures**: Displays the current and maximum temperatures reported by the motor • **Status**: Indicates the motor status and current activity • **Tension**: Applies a brief smooth tension to the motor to take up any slack • **Shake**: Identifies the motor by shaking it aggressively • **Assign...**: Applies the ID to the currently connected motor

data.name: SABT_Text_Connection
data.value: 1. Select a **Serial Port** from the drop-down list below. Only ports that appear to be the belt tensioner device will be shown. If the list is empty, check that the controller is plugged in. It should appear even without power or any motors connected 2. Connect a single motor (or unplug the power connectors on all but one motor) and click **Assign ID 1** 3. Disconnect that motor, connect the next motor and click **Assign ID 2** 4. Disconnect that motor, connect the next motor and click **Assign ID 3** (where using 3+ motors) 5. Disconnect that motor, connect the next motor and click **Assign ID 3** (where using 4 motors) 6. Reconnect all motors and click **Detect Motors** 7. Allocate motors to belts under the **Mapping** column and set rotation directions under **Direction**

data.name: SABT_Text_IdleTension
data.value: • Always applied while not driving (no effect while driving) • Behaves like the retraction spring on an inertia reel belt • Set to zero to disable; limited to 25% of maximum motor torque

data.name: SABT_Text_DrivingTension
data.value: • The minimum and maximum tension to be applied while driving • Increasing the minimum will apply a constant tension and enhance acceleration and jumping effects • Reducing the maximum will result in a reduction of overall tension strength

data.name: SABT_Text_TensionStep
data.value: • How much the above tension values change when adjusted via SimHub 'Actions' • Useful when using control hardware like encoder knobs with variable step counts

data.name: SABT_Text_HorizontalBias
data.value: • If tension feels unbalanced between sides, adjust this left or right to bias towards that side • Check and correct your belt path and contact points before resorting to using this setting

data.name: SABT_Text_VerticalBias
data.value: • If you've mapped motors to both the waist and shoulder belts, you can adjust the relative force bias between these

data.name: SABT_Text_Cornering
data.value: • How much cornering forces should affect the tension differential between the two belts

data.name: SABT_Text_Braking
data.value: • How much deceleration forces should increase the tension on both belts

data.name: SABT_Text_Acceleration
data.value: • How much acceleration forces should decrease the tension on both belts • Set minimum 'Driving Tension' to non-zero for best results (see 'Tension' tab)

data.name: SABT_Text_Jumping
data.value: • How much jumping should decrease the tension on both belts • Set minimum 'Driving Tension' to non-zero for best results (see 'Tension' tab)

data.name: SABT_Text_Landing
data.value: • How much landing should increase the tension on both belts

data.name: SABT_Text_Engine
data.value: • To what extent low-speed engine idle and stalling vibrations should be felt through the belts • This effect is based upon the reported engine speed and is limited to low-RPMs due to motor limitations

data.name: SABT_Text_Upshifting
data.value: • Adds a more pronounced tension blip on upshift • Customize the effect by providing a sequence of space-separated `{milliseconds}:{torque%}` values in the field above • Milliseconds values are relative to the start of the shift, while torque values are 0 to 100 (%) • `0ms:100% 200ms:100% 500ms:0%` would equate to `Start at 100% torque, stay there until 200ms, then fade down to 0% torque between 200ms and 500ms` • `0ms:0% 100ms:100% 300ms:100% 600ms:0%` would equate to `Start at 0% torque, fade up to 100% at 100ms, hold until 300ms, then fade down to 0% torque between 300ms and 500ms`

data.name: SABT_Text_Profiles
data.value: • With 'Auto-Switching' enabled, tuning profiles are automatically loaded for the current game (and vehicle class, where known), with the most specific profile taking priority • Copying an existing profile will result in its tuning parameters being loaded into a new profile for the currently active game (and vehicle class, where known) • Vehicle class profiles cannot be created if the game does not report a vehicle class or model • Changes made to profiles are automatically saved

data.name: SABT_Text_Tuning
data.value: • With 'Auto-Tuning' enabled, the slider values below will automatically adjust to match the values from the replayed telemetry • For ease of tuning, use a previously recorded game replay (optionally with the specific vehicle class to tune for) • Motor output is disabled during tuning for safety reasons • 'Auto-Switching' will be automatically disabled when using the automatic tuning feature • 'Auto-Tuning' will be automatically disabled if the active profile changes

data.name: SABT_Text_Preferences
data.value: These settings are not game-specific and control the basic operation of the tensioner; including overall output both during and between game sessions. They should be set to your liking before performing fine-tuning within the 'Profiles' tab.

data.name: SABT_Text_TemperatureThrottlingRange
data.value: • The motors should not get hot during operation; but they are capable of operating at up to 80°C • Depending on your choice of filament, your printed parts may fail at lower temperatures (PLA <60°C, PETG <85°C, ABS <95°C) • The first slider sets the temperature at which thermal throttling should start (a reduction in motor power) • The second slider sets the temperature at which the motors should be disabled to prevent damage • While between these temperatures, the motor output will be gradually reduced (proportional to the temperature)

data.name: SABT_Text_Telemetry
data.value: • Adjust these ranges **before anything else**, as they control the overall mapping of telemetry forces to belt tension • Use **Auto-Tuning** to set these automatically, or adjust manually by observing plotted telemetry data during a replay • These should equal the **maximum forces** you expect your vehicle to experience under normal gameplay

data.name: SABT_Text_Smoothing
data.value: • How much the belt tension output should be smoothed • This does not apply to all effects (such as **Engine RPM**), as that would make them ineffective

data.name: SABT_Text_Diagnostics
data.value: If you are having connectivity, thermal or reliability issues with your installation, the data below may be helpful. Note that 'Faults' numbers under 10 are considered to be normal and do not affect operation of the tensioner. However higher numbers may indicate a problem with the power supply, USB cable or hub, motor connectors, etc
